stem: Veer has one $5$ cm by $3$ cm rectangle. He cuts it into two pieces along a mid-line parallel to the $3$ cm side and then rejoins the pieces along a different edge.

parts.text: Which claim about perimeter is correct?

options.text: The perimeter must stay $16$ cm, because the same pieces are used.
The new outline can have a different perimeter even though the pieces are the same.
The perimeter always becomes half of $16$ cm after any cut.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that compares the outer edges before and after rejoining.

part_answers.answer: Edges that were outer can become joined and disappear from the outline, or new outer edges can appear, so perimeter can change with the same pieces.

teacher.key_rationale: Same pieces do not lock perimeter; joining hides edges and can change the outline length. Halving always is false.
